title: Spot the mistake: composing a printer
idea: Composing functions: the classic bug — feeding a sub-plan that PRINTS (returns None) into another call. Diagnose and fix.

options: double returns None, so add_one(None) + 1 fails
exercises.explanation: double prints 10 but returns None. So add_one gets None, and None + 1 errors. The inner sub-plan must RETURN.
The inner sub-plan must hand back a value, so use return. Then add_one(10) is 11.

exercises.prompt: To compose, the INNER sub-plan must return a value — a printing one gives None.
exercises.explanation: Yes. The outer call needs a real argument. A printing inner call feeds None, which usually breaks the outer call.
return n * 2 hands back the value so add_one(double(5)) becomes add_one(10) = 11.
Now double(5)=10 and add_one(10)=11. Both sub-plans return, so composing works.

options: show returns None, so add(2, None) fails
exercises.explanation: show prints 3 but returns None. add(2, None) tries 2 + None, which errors. show shouldn't feed add.

exercises.prompt: What's the clue that composing failed?
options: A None shows up, or an error about adding None
exercises.explanation: None (or a 'None + number' error) signals that a composed inner call printed instead of returning.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: which sub-plan is safe to feed into another call?
exercises.explanation: Only the one that returns a real value can be composed. The others give None.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a CORRECT composition: define double (returns), define add_one (returns), print add_one(double(6)).
exercises.explanation: Both sub-plans return, so double(6)=12 feeds add_one -> 13. No None in sight.

options: Don't compose a sub-plan that prints — the inner call must return a value
exercises.explanation: Composing needs returned values. A printing inner call hands back None and breaks the chain.
